FIX ROUND 697d for story #697 slice A (a personal recipe shelf beside host.json; #432's first slice), on branch story-697-personal-shelf, already checked out in this worktree at 4d44d03f.

You are fixing exactly the finding below and its CLASS, nothing beside them. Decision 0071 (the architectural principles) is ACCEPTED. Build to it. This is the third security hold on one class, "a shelf path judged in one spelling and read in another". Close the class by construction, not this one spelling.

HISTORY OF THE BRANCH (cut from main 0428e57f; your diff is judged against it)
- 3e1efab4 (story run implement-story-697-recipes-a-pe-b21b3ebf): slice A: places::personal_shelf; recipes/personal.rs (`recipes add --personal`, personal::holding resolving `--recipe` on run, resume, rerun, queue add and `recipes show` with Unshelved::Shadowed for a name on both shelves); `recipes list`'s origin column; doctor's personal lines; decision 0083's third addendum (Status: proposed). Review: SECURITY-HOLD (`--recipe x/` bypassed Shadowed).
- 95234fda (fix round 697b): `--recipe` names a recipe, never a path (Unshelved::Unplain); recipes::add takes a typed Origin; the personal install judges no library mark at its own shelf. Review: SECURITY-HOLD (an unreadable shelf read as an empty one).
- 4d44d03f (fix round 697c): holding_in judges both shelves through personal::resolving before either name probe; places::resolved (pub, new) is the one absent / dangling / not-a-directory judgement, shared with default_map (MapDangling, MapNotAFile and Unreadable kept); Unshelved::Unread is typed; Origin::place resolves the install shelf for both origins; refuse_folder consumes Resolved and recipes::standing is gone (recipes.rs 800 -> 781). Review: SECURITY-HOLD again, below.
- When you are done, the branch is the above plus ONE new commit of yours. Do not rebase, squash or amend.

FIX THIS, proved by binding tests with exact text and removal controls (plant the shape, see the test fail with the stated text, remove the plant):

1. HIGH, security (decision 0071 ruling 3, a path untyped at the edge; the house fail-closed rule; #697 ruling 2). A SLASH-SUFFIXED explicit shelf spelling bypasses the unreadable-shelf refusal. The review's reproduction on the HEAD binary: `x` on .brokkr/recipes and on <config>/brokkr/recipes; then .brokkr/recipes replaced by a symbolic link to an absent target. The default spelling and `--dir .brokkr/recipes` refuse Unread (exit 1), but `recipes show x --dir .brokkr/recipes/` exits 0 and prints the PERSONAL bundle, and so do `--dir .brokkr/recipes/.`, `--dir ./.brokkr/recipes/` and the absolute path with a trailing slash. `run --recipe x --recipes-dir .brokkr/recipes/ --feature probe --no-view` exits 0 and runs the personal recipe; `queue add ... --recipe x --recipes-dir .brokkr/recipes/` exits 0 and queues it. (`--dir .brokkr//recipes` refuses correctly.) Trailing slashes come from shell completion and scripts.
   Cause: personal::resolving (personal.rs ~:82-110) walks shelf.ancestors() on the path AS SPELLED; places::resolved (places.rs ~:501-506) calls symlink_metadata on "<link>/", which the kernel resolves THROUGH the trailing slash, so a dangling link reads NotFound and is judged absent; Path::parent then skips the unsuffixed link and lands on the readable parent .brokkr, after which stands() probes "<shelf>/x" through the dangling link and reads x as absent, so the personal recipe wins alone.
   Fix, by construction: a shelf path is NORMALISED ONCE, at the edge, before anything judges or reads it, and every judgement and every read takes the normalised value. Normalised means: rebuilt from its components (`Path::components()` collected), so no trailing separator, no `.` component and no doubled separator; a `..` component is kept as spelled (lexical `..` folding is not equivalent through links) and is judged by places::resolved like any other entry. Give it a type (decision 0071 ruling 3), for example a `Shelf` newtype whose only constructor normalises, so a raw spelling cannot reach resolving, places::resolved, stands, holding_in, Origin::place, `recipes show`, `recipes list` or doctor. `--dir`, `--recipes-dir`, the folder's default shelf (folder::Layout) and places::personal_shelf all enter through it. places::resolved itself must never call symlink_metadata on a spelling with a trailing separator: if it can receive one, normalise there too, and bind it.
   - THE CLASS: sweep every function in recipes.rs, recipes/*.rs, places.rs, folder.rs, verbs/setup.rs, verbs/delivery.rs and doctor/folder.rs that judges or reads a shelf or a recipe directory by a path (symlink_metadata, metadata, read_dir, canonicalize, places::entry, places::resolved, is_dir, join of a name onto a shelf). For each, say in notes which spelling it receives now and how. If any can still receive a raw spelling, route it through the type.
   - Tests (exact text), extending shelf::a_shelf_that_cannot_be_read_refuses_on_every_verb's table: for a DANGLING project shelf link AND a project shelf that is a regular FILE, the explicit spellings `.brokkr/recipes/`, `.brokkr/recipes/.`, `./.brokkr/recipes/`, `.brokkr//recipes` and the absolute path with a trailing slash, through `recipes show --dir` and `--recipes-dir` on run, resume, rerun and queue add, with `x` on both shelves and with `x` on the personal shelf alone. Each exits 1 with the exact Unread text, no run is started, no queue entry is written, and neither fake driver's state changes. Pin ONE cause text for the file shape across every spelling (the review saw 'Not a directory (os error 20)' through the slash and 'not a directory' without; one judgement means one text). A unit test constructs the type from each spelling and asserts they are equal, and a unit test of resolving with a trailing-slash shelf matches Unshelved::Unread by variant. Removal control: bypass the normalisation (construct the type from the raw spelling) and see `recipes show x --dir .brokkr/recipes/` exit 0 and the test fail.

2. INFO, take it if the type makes it free (decision 0071 ruling 5): `recipes list` and doctor warn about an unreadable shelf through read_dir and places::entry, not places::resolved, so a shelf whose path passes through an unreadable ancestor lists as empty where resolution refuses. If list and doctor take the same type and the same judgement without changing their warning lines' text, do it and say so; otherwise leave them and say why.

CARRY, do not change (each goes in your notes for the PR):
- The configuration assumption (XDG_CONFIG_HOME inside a repository is the operator's own choice; no refusal; the addendum states it).
- Choice (g): a queued launch keeps the shelf it resolved at queue time, so a shadow or a break that arises later is not rechecked at dispatch (LOW).
- Public API growth: `pub fn places::personal_shelf` and `pub fn places::resolved` (and, if the shelf type must be public, that one item; keep it to one).
- `recipes list` appends the personal shelf beside an explicit `--dir` listing (choice (b)); choices (a), (e), (f); tests/doc_samples.rs and tests/contributing.rs run `recipes list` without a hermetic XDG_CONFIG_HOME; quickstart.md's list samples lack the origin column (#720 holds both files: do not edit them); `add --personal` does not refuse at install a name the project shelf already holds (resolution refuses it).
- Slice B stays a follow-up.
- Decision 0083's third addendum: add the normalisation as one sentence beside the Unread refusal ("every spelling of one shelf is judged at the same entry"), and change nothing else in it.

For the implement phase: fix, then run, all clean, from the worktree root: cargo fmt --all -- --check; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings; cargo test -p brokkr-cli --lib --locked -- recipes:: folder:: verbs:: doctor::; cargo test -p brokkr-cli --test it --locked -- shelf:: recipes:: brokkr_folder:: init_doctor:: doc_truth:: doc_samples:: decisions_index:: suppressions:: contributing::; cargo test -p brokkr-cli --lib --locked cli_reference; cargo test -p brokkr-runtime --lib --locked -- places:: admission::; typos --hidden; quality/ratchet.sh files, clones and api; `cargo crap --path crates/brokkr-cli/src --format json` and `cargo crap --path crates/brokkr-runtime/src --format json` for every function you add or grow (CC at most max(15, its quality/crap-baseline.json row); a new or moved function at most 15); git diff --check. Crate-scope every run: the whole brokkr-cli suite can hang. Do not run scripts/coverage-exact.sh; the controller runs it. A new test file is named *_tests.rs or tests.rs. Integration tests set XDG_CONFIG_HOME and HOME on the child Command, never on the test process. recipes.rs stays at or under 800 lines.

Every review position, panel member or chief, is READ-ONLY: it changes no tracked file and makes no commit, whatever this text asks. It reports each finding. Only the implement phase fixes a finding the review returns. Reviewers: besides judging this fix, try every other spelling of a shelf path you can think of (relative, absolute, `..` through a link, a link to a link, a shelf under a linked ancestor) against both shelves, and report any that reaches a recipe the default spelling refuses.

Commit one signed-off commit (git commit -s), message "recipes: <what changed> (#697)" in the repository's style, ending with the line "Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>". Never push. Run every command in the foreground and wait for it: never background a command or schedule a wake-up, because a headless seat ends when it waits.

Threat model (operator ruling, 2026-09-26): catch realistic accidental misuse, and fail closed on what cannot be read. A deliberate, exotic evasion is a LOW residual.

HOST FACTS AND PARALLEL WORK
- Main is origin/main as you find it (29e89486 or later). Main lands only through the merge queue. Do not merge or rebase main.
- READ these whole before you start: recipes/personal.rs and its tests; places.rs's entry, absent, resolved and default_map; folder.rs's Layout recipes and shelf; verbs/setup.rs and verbs/delivery.rs's shelf handling; 4d44d03f's commit message.

- Test modules: the exact-coverage gate leaves out only files named tests.rs or *_tests.rs / *-tests.rs. The doc_truth and suppressions scanners read TRACKED files only: `git add -N` a new file before running them.
- Other work runs in parallel. Stay out of it:
  - Decision 0065 slice two (the-forge-b9; NEVER message it, or any brokkr-wt-* seat) runs U7d3 (adapters/*.json, protocol adapters.rs, runtime capabilities/binding.rs; it re-blesses every witness digest) and owns engine*, crates/brokkr-protocol, and brokkr-cli cli_args.rs, doctor.rs and doctor/capabilities.rs. This round touches none of them. If `--dir`/`--recipes-dir`'s type must change in cli_args.rs (DeliveryArgs), convert at the edge in verbs/delivery.rs instead.
  - #365 slice 3 (PR #720) holds tests/doc_samples.rs, tests/init_stacks.rs, tests/init_doctor.rs and the guides quickstart.md, the five starters and versioning.md.

instructions.analyze:
# OpenSpec analyze

Judge duplication, ambiguity, underspecification, house alignment, coverage gaps, and inconsistency across proposal, deltas, design and tasks. Treat the realm house as the constitution. Return each finding with severity and its earliest owning artifact; zero findings is consistent.
instructions.clarify:
# OpenSpec clarify

Judge underspecified areas, unquantified language, missing decisions, capability/delta mismatches, and requirements without adequate scenarios. Return every ambiguity with the evidence needed to settle it; zero findings is clear.
instructions.design:
# OpenSpec design

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/design.md`. Record context, goals and non-goals, decisions with alternatives, risks, migration, and open questions. On return, revise the design and dependent artifacts so no finding is merely acknowledged.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.
instructions.implement:
# OpenSpec tasks

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/tasks.md` as numbered groups of checkboxes. Name the requirement served by every task. On return, repair the breakdown and its requirement coverage before implementation resumes.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.

Change location: `openspec/changes/{change}`. Archive operation: ["openspec","archive","{change}","--yes"].

# OpenSpec archive

Folding a change is the last task: run the archive operation named above,
which moves the change directory under `openspec/changes/archive/` and
folds its deltas into `openspec/specs/`. Folding also records which change
wrote which capability, so every capability the change touched carries a
`## Provenance` list.

After the archive operation, open each capability's
`openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` that the change touched and append
exactly one line under a `## Provenance` heading held at the end of the
file:

`- \`<archived-directory-name>\` — folded <YYYY-MM-DD>`

`<archived-directory-name>` is the directory the archive operation
created under `openspec/changes/archive/`; `<YYYY-MM-DD>` is the day it
was folded. Append only: never rewrite, reorder or remove an existing
provenance line, because standing truth accumulates and is not edited into
a different meaning. The line is a pointer, not a summary — it names the
change and nothing else, and the why stays in the change directory.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, and `reference/` (its schemas included) are
read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `recipes/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

The supported hosts are Linux and macOS (decision 0063); WSL2 is Linux. Write
no Windows-conditional code, test or evidence.

## Architecture

Decision 0071 rules how code here is shaped. Build to it, and cite its ruling
numbers in what you judge. Where a gate named below holds a rule, the gate is
the authority, and a finding it would catch is the gate's.

- **Pure core (ruling 1).** `brokkr-core` and `brokkr-view` do no I/O and read
  no clock, environment or randomness. They run no process. Pass `now`, paths
  and environment in as arguments. Effects live in the crates above core and
  view, and are journaled.
- **Enums and data, not traits (ruling 2).** A closed set is an enum matched
  exhaustively, with no wildcard arm that decides behaviour. Anything an
  operator extends is data under `adapters/`, `agents/`, `recipes/` or
  `realms.json`, validated and digested. Add a trait only for a seam whose
  contract spans several operations that must stay consistent with one
  another, reached across a process or service boundary, and name that seam
  in its doc comment. `ProducerTransport` is the one such trait today. A test
  double alone does not make a seam: a single substitutable function is a
  closure seam (`*_with`, `*_in`), which is how the house inverts a
  dependency otherwise.
- **Typed at the edge (ruling 3).** Parse wire, file and harness data once
  into a type, with `serde` and `deny_unknown_fields` where the contract is
  closed. `serde_json::Value` never goes past the edge, into state, or back
  out by string key. Never put `format!("{:?}")` in anything digested or
  journaled. A doubly-optional field or a string vocabulary is a missing enum.
- **Small functions (ruling 4).** New and changed functions stay within 100
  lines, nesting depth 5 and 7 parameters. Cyclomatic complexity follows
  the operator's 2026-09-26 ruling: a function may reach the higher of 15
  and its baseline, so a new function stays within 15, an existing one may
  change freely up to 15, and one already over 15 may only shrink.
  Production files stay within 800 lines and test files within 2,000, and a
  file already over may not grow. Add no new `jscpd` clone in production
  code, test code or data. `quality/` holds the measured baseline. Today's
  offenders carry `#[allow(clippy::…)]`, and #337 converts them to
  `#[expect(clippy::…, reason = "…")]`. Add a suppression only by a ruling,
  and remove it when you fix the function. A new suppression is
  `#[expect(…, reason)]`, never `#[allow]`.
- **Once (ruling 5).** Every fact has one home. A repeated vocabulary, skeleton
  or helper becomes one function or one table. An agent is defined once under
  `agents/`, and seats hire it by reference. A recipe that differs from another
  by a model, a seat or an entry is an `extends` overlay, never a copy. The
  agent library does not yet accept `extends`, and #360 builds it. Until then,
  a variation of an agent lives at the seat that hires it, overridden in a
  recipe overlay. It is never a second agent file that restates the first. A
  copy that must exist, such as a script a bundle pins, is held to its source
  by a test.
- **Nothing unused (ruling 6).** Add no alias, agent, contract version, flag or
  `pub` item without a consumer, and prefer `pub(crate)`. A deprecation names
  the release that removes it.
- **One derivation (ruling 7).** A fact shown on two surfaces is derived once
  in `brokkr-view`. The CLI, the TUI and `ui.html` only paint it. The engine
  never admits anything by a display-crate function.
- **Typed errors (ruling 8).** Return a `thiserror` enum whose `Display` keeps
  the operator's text. Tests match variants and pin each module's text once.
  Add no new `Result<_, String>`.
- **Tests that bind (ruling 9).** Assert exact values or variants, never
  `is_err()` alone. Show that every new test binds: a compiling mutation that
  removes the behaviour must make it fail. Restore the behaviour and record
  the failing test. Share fixtures through builders. Never change the process
  environment without a guard that restores it on unwind. A production guard
  left out because the exact-coverage gate would count it unreachable carries
  a removal-control test for the invariant that makes it unreachable, and the
  comment explaining the omission names that test.
- **The house's patterns (ruling 10).**
  - A harness is a module behind `AdapterKind`. This is the target form;
    today all five kinds share one module, and #347 and #348 build the
    split.
  - A CLI verb is a `Cmd` variant plus a handler.
  - A long parameter list becomes a parameter object.
  - Argv and mount tables are built with a builder.
  - Observing the world is split from deciding on it.
  - Never use a trait-object registry for a closed set.

Judges rate a finding against these rulings by this table, and cite the ruling
number:

- **info:** something a house gate would catch. The gate's verdict is the
  authority.
- **low:** a new or changed function over a ceiling, a rule written a second
  time, an item added without a consumer, or a `Value` carried past its edge
  within one module.
- **medium:** an untyped vocabulary that crosses crates, recipe or agent data
  copied instead of extended, a fact derived a second time on another surface,
  an error matched by its text, or a new test that cannot fail.
- **high or above:** any violation that hides a fail-open path or weakens a
  refusal. It is carried as a security finding.

A principle the implementer bent knowingly, and named with its reason in
`notes`, is still rated, and the judge carries that reason with the finding.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.


result.notes:
Fix round 697d, one signed-off commit cca4e2f6 on 4d44d03f (no rebase, squash or amend; not pushed).

FINDING 1 (HIGH), closed by construction. A shelf path now has a type, recipes::personal::ShelfPath (pub(crate), so no public API growth). Its only constructor rebuilds the path from Path::components() with CurDir filtered out: no trailing separator, no `.`, no doubled separator. A `..` stays as spelled. A spelling of `.` alone becomes `.`, and an empty spelling stays empty. Every edge enters through it: Layout::recipes, Layout::listing and Layout::install_shelf (covering --dir on recipes list/show, --recipes-dir on run/resume/rerun/queue add via delivery.rs, the folder default .brokkr/recipes and <root>/recipes) and personal::shelf (places::personal_shelf). cli_args.rs is untouched. places::resolved also normalises internally, so it never calls symlink_metadata on a trailing-separator spelling; that is bound by places_tests::an_entry_is_resolved_whatever_its_spelling.

CLASS SWEEP (the spelling each function receives now):
- personal.rs: resolving, holding, holding_in, Origin::place, list and add take &ShelfPath or ShelfPath. holding_in's stands() joins the plain name onto the normalised shelf. Made::above gets shelf.path() from ShelfPath.
